questions.question: The circuit shown in figure is said to be in common configuration.
questions.explanation: In the given circuit, the input signal is applied to the base terminal and the output is taken from the emitter terminal. The collector terminal is common to both the input and output circuits through the DC supply. Hence, the transistor is operating in the common collector (CC) configuration, also known as an emitter follower. \[\boxed{\textbf{Common Collector (CC) Configuration}}\]

questions.question:
If A and B are inputs to a logic gate, then match the logic with its output
(a) NAND;;;;;; (i) \(\overline{\bar A + \bar B}\)
(b) NOR;;;;;; (ii) \(\bar A + \bar B\)
(c) XNOR;;;;;; (iii) \(\bar A \bar B + AB\)

options: a - ii , b - i , c - iii , d - iv
a - ii , b - iv , c - iii , d - i
a - i , b - iv , c - ii , d - iii
a - iii , b - ii , c - iv , d - i
questions.explanation:
If A and B are inputs to a logic gate, then the logic according to its output is shown:
NOR;;;;;; \(\bar A . \bar B\)
NAND;;;;;; \(\bar A + \bar B\)

questions.ref: Representation of Boolean Expressions and K-Maps Q1
questions.question: A combination circuit has inputs \(A,B\) and \(C\) and its Karnaugh Map is given in figure. The output of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: From the K-Map, it is observed that no quads or pairs can be formed. Thus the Boolean expression obtained is: \[Y = (A \bar B + \bar AB)\bar C + (\bar A \bar B + AB)C\] \[Y = (A \oplus B) \bar C + \overline{(A \oplus B)} C = A \oplus B \oplus C\] \[\boxed{(C)\;A \oplus B \oplus C}\]

questions.question: The combinatorial circuit shown in figure employs a 4x1 multiplexer. The output \(Q\) of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: From the given circuit , inputs are \[D_0 = 1 \;\; \;\;,  \;\;\;\;  D_1 =1 \;\; \;\;,  \;\;\;\;  D_2 =1 \;\; \;\;,  \;\;\;\;  D_3 = C\] Selection lines are \[S_1 = A\;\; \;\;,  \;\;\;\; S_0 = B\] Thus final output equation is: \[Q = \bar S_1 \bar S_0 D_0 + \bar S_1 S_0 D_1 + S_1 \bar S_0 D_2 + S_1 S_0 D_3\] \[Q = \bar A \bar BC + \bar A B + A \bar B +AB = \bar A (\bar BC + B) + A  (\bar B +B)\] \[Q = \bar A (B+C) + A = A+B+C\] \[\boxed{(B) \; A+B+C}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.ref: Block Diagram and Signal Flow Graph Q1
questions.question: For the signal flow graph show in figure, the transfer function is \(C(s)/R(s) =\) .
questions.note: No single correct answer in the official key
questions.explanation:
To find the overall closed-loop transfer function of the given signal flow graph, we apply Mason's Gain Formula:
  • Forward path: \(P_1 = G_1 G_2 G_3\)
  • Individual loops: \(L_1 = -G_1 G_2 H_1\), \(L_2 = -G_2 G_3 H_2\)
Since both loops touch the single forward path, the path factor is \(\Delta_1 = 1 - 0 = 1\). There are no non-touching loops, so the system determinant \(\Delta\) is given by: \[\Delta = 1 - (L_1 + L_2) = 1 + G_1 G_2 H_1 + G_2 G_3 H_2\] Applying Mason's Gain Formula: \[\text{T.F.} = \frac{P_1\Delta_1}{\Delta} = \frac{G_1 G_2 G_3 (1 - 0)}{1 + G_1 G_2 H_1 + G_2 G_3 H_2}\] \[\boxed{\frac{G_1 G_2 G_3}{1 + G_1 G_2 H_1 + G_2 G_3 H_2}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The break away point of the root locus on the real axis for a closed-loop system with a loop gain \(G(s) H(s) =  \dfrac{K(s + 10)}{(s + 2)(s + 5)}\) lies
questions.explanation: Given open-loop transfer function: \[G(s)H(s) = \frac{K(s + 10)}{(s + 2)(s + 5)}\] The open-loop poles are at \(s = -2, -5\) and the open-loop zero is at \(s = -10\). Since the segment between the two open-loop poles \(s = -2\) and \(s = -5\) lies entirely on the root locus, the branches must break away from each other within this interval. Therefore, without calculating the exact derivative, the breakaway point must lie between \(-2\) and \(-5\) \[\boxed{\text{(B) between $-2$ and $-5$}}\]
